evidence.source: 中央研究院漢字構形資料庫
evidence.field: 字形演變; 甲骨文合集8159; 金文集成04140; 說文小篆
evidence.text: The catalog lists 休 in an oracle-bone example (合集8159), a bronze example (集成04140), and the Shuowen seal-script category. Its analysis identifies the left component as a person in profile and the right as 木 ‘tree,’ interpreting the graph as a person leaning beside a tree to rest. These are catalog identifications and an interpretation; the cited artifact dates and semantic reading were not independently verified.
evidence.title: 漢字「休」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.field: 形義通解; early forms and graph analysis
evidence.text: The entry analyzes the early graph as 人 plus 木, with the person’s back against the trunk. It says some tree tops slant toward the person to suggest shade; despite resemblance to 禾, it identifies the component as 木. Its catalog shows an oracle-bone form, bronze forms, and later script categories. This supports the traditional interpretation, but is a scholarly analysis rather than an independently established reading of every inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.text: 《字通》 disputes the person-resting-beside-a-tree interpretation. It proposes that the 木-like element was originally 禾-shaped and represented paired marker posts at a military gate, and that 休 referred to recognition of military merit before them. It cites a bronze inscription phrase glossed ‘good/commendable.’ It also reports Guo Moruo’s different rest-in-a-field proposal, which it criticizes. This is a material disagreement; the inspected page does not settle it against the competing graph analysis.
evidence.title: 休(キュウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: 《說文解字》 as transcribed by 漢典
evidence.field: 休; 說文解字 and 說文解字注
evidence.text: The transmitted Shuowen defines 休 as ‘cease/rest’ (息止也) and explains its graph as 从人依木, ‘from a person relying on a tree/wood’; it records 庥 as an alternate form with 广. This is an early lexicographic account, not direct proof of the graph’s original motivation.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.field: 形義通解; cited textual and bronze-inscription uses
evidence.text: The entry proposes semantic extensions from tree shade to shelter/protection, then to benefaction or reward; it associates resting under shade with pleasure and goodness, and separately links resting with stopping. It cites bronze inscriptions including 剌鼎, 效卣, 員鼎 and 噩侯鼎, alongside received texts such as 詩經 and 漢書. These attestations support multiple uses, but the source’s proposed semantic links do not establish a securely dated order of development. The entry says 茠 differentiated the shade sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

evidence.field: 休 詳細解釋; cited textual examples
evidence.text: The entry records traditional rest/stopping examples including 《詩·周南·漢廣》 ‘南有喬木，不可休思’, 《詩·大雅·民勞》 ‘汔可小休’, and 《禮記·月令》 ‘毋休於都’; it also cites shelter/protection in the 《漢書·王莽傳》注. These examples attest uses in received texts, but they do not establish which sense came first or independently date the composition of each passage.
evidence.title: 休 xiū、xù、xǔ — 漢典

evidence.source: Kotobank, 精選版 日本国語大辞典
evidence.field: やすらい; やすまり; やすめ entries
evidence.text: The entry gives dated Japanese lexical examples for words written 休: やすらい ‘hesitation’ in 蜻蛉日記 (c. 974), やすまり ‘rest/support’ in 栄花物語 (1028–92), and a rest command やすめ in a 1881 military vocabulary. These date cited Japanese word uses, not the origin of the graph or the Chinese semantic sequence.
evidence.title: 休(キュウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.text: Unicode’s Unihan documentation lists kMandarin among the database properties. This establishes the property’s scope but does not provide the requested character-specific values for 休, 木 or 人.
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

evidence.text: Exact local rows give U+4F11 休 kMandarin xiū; U+6728 木 kMandarin mù; and U+4EBA 人 kMandarin rén. These are current-reading metadata, not external evidence or evidence for an ancient sound relation. The official character-specific Unicode record URLs were attempted but inaccessible in this research session.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan record U+4F11 (attempted; inaccessible)

evidence.text: The exact local rows give 休 xiū, Middle Chinese xjuw, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *qʰ(r)u, for the glosses ‘rest (v.)’ and ‘blessing.’ These readings pertain to 休, not a proposed sound component. No inspected analysis in this research proposes 人 or 木 as phonetic in this graph.
evidence.title: 漢典 reading entry for 休; external click-through for readings

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, CUHK Humanum
evidence.text: This account treats 人 and 木 as semantic components and does not propose a phonetic component. Thus no component-to-host ancient sound match is asserted or required by this analysis. The military-gate proposal also does not establish a distinct sound component. No whole-graph phonetic-loan account was found in the inspected sources.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 休

search_audit.outcome: Refined search for semantic attestations and early-use limits; inspected the CUHK page again and found a Sinica article result about 西周 bronze uses, including reward and benefaction. The article was not opened, so its details are not used as verified evidence.

gaps: Neither this inspection nor the sources establish a securely dated semantic chronology. Oracle-bone and bronze catalog entries identify graph examples, but their individual dates, readings, and contexts were not independently verified from primary inscription records here.

The person-plus-tree/rest interpretation and the military marker-post interpretation conflict over the right-hand component’s identity and original motivation. No primary inscription context inspected here resolves the disagreement; no glyph image was visually inspected.

The earliest attested lexical sense cannot be ranked confidently from dictionary gloss lists. The sources connect rest, shade, protection, benefaction, goodness, reward, stopping and ‘do not’ in proposed ways, but the links and chronology remain partly uncertain.

The specific official Unihan records for U+4F11, U+6728 and U+4EBA could not be opened because the web tool returned internal errors. Local Unihan rows were checked but cannot serve as external click-through evidence.

No researched source proposes a sound component or a whole-graph phonetic loan for 休. 人 and 木 readings were checked locally, but ancient component sound comparisons are not applicable to the reviewed semantic analyses.
